## Goal (user story)
As a proxy operator, when a long agent session runs, its requests must keep progressing. A request must never sit in a remote fallback tier for 15 minutes and die with a 900-second timeout, and must never be blocked by local slot-accounting errors.

## Symptoms observed 2026-09-14
- pi session herdr-1789404733-1187468-16836 received "We were unable to start processing your request within the 900-second timeout limit. Please try again later." six times between 19:18 and 20:46 (about 17-18 min apart).
- dispatch_first_byte_ms: p50 4.6 s, p90 40 s, p99 212 s, max 713 s.
- 1982 routing_skip_local reason=context_too_large, 2341 fallbacks, 503 local_dispatch_denied, 811 counter-recovery warnings.

## Root causes (diagnosed this session)
1. Local dispatch accounting resets the generating counter mid-stream on a 1-slot backend (LP-0MU1RXEGB002CAL4).
2. Remote fallback stalls 240 s on opencode-go and retries empty upstream responses without a bound (LP-0MU1RXEPL005CK97).
3. The local large-context routing threshold does not scale with the per-slot capacity now that the profile runs one slot (LP-0MU1RXF6R004S8XL).
4. Proxy compaction fails 100 percent (summarizer_failed) and pushes sessions to remote_with_guidance (LP-0MU1RXEY10075TUU).

## Related existing work - do NOT duplicate
- LP-0MTXCQA8I0038J4X [CRITICAL] Dedicated small summarizer model for proxy-side session compaction - in-progress. This is the specialist model item; the compaction root cause above is largely owned by it plus the items below.
- LP-0MTT0O74N009E7N2 Add 'compact' model (Muse to DeepSeek) and wire proxy-side compaction to it - in-progress.
- LP-0MTVJF5HU007ISP1 Fix local summarizer timeout causing compaction failures - blocked by LP-0MTT0PB6J0053BPP.
- LP-0MTT0PB6J0053BPP Increase compaction_summarizer_timeout to 120s - open.
- LP-0MTY8Y1VB006IYGQ Per-model compaction trigger configuration - open.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No request in a 24 h post-change window returns the upstream 900-second queue-timeout error.
- [ ] dispatch_first_byte_ms p99 is below 60 s for local-routed requests.
- [ ] Zero local_generating_queries counter-recovery false positives while a stream is in flight.
- [ ] Compaction succeeds and is durable for sessions above the trigger (coordinates with the specialist model item rather than reimplementing it).
- [ ] The large-context routing threshold is an intentional, documented value for the 1-slot profile.
- [ ] Full test suite green.

## Non-goals
- Adding a new summariser model (owned by LP-0MTXCQA8I0038J4X).
- Renaming deepseek model identifiers (LP-0MU1RXFNO00552VR, pending a scope decision).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRIKWYHM008LVLP** – Fix _get_local_concurrency_info to use session_slot_pool_size instead of local_max_concurrent_queries (completed)
- **LP-0MSUDM2MI009M335** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/skill/cleanup/scripts/prune_local_branches.py:38 — Unused `noqa` directive (non-enabled: `BLE001`) (RUF100) (completed)
- **LP-0MSHW2AXJ009DO3S** – Fix /slots endpoint query: llama-server returns HTTP 400 without ?model=, so /llama/local/status always reports 0/0 slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounting, add, adding, again (+131 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounting, add, adding, again (+131 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, accounting, add, adding, again (+131 more)
data.title: Fix the proxy: large-context sessions stall and time out instead of progressing

# Exhaustion diagnostics: expose usage-limit quarantine and derive retry_after from it

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO

## Problem

`_log_exhausted_providers` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4106`) only inspects entry-name and
brand cooldowns, so accounts quarantined by `usage_limit_reset_pending`
(`_usage_reset_at`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py:3190`) are invisible. During the overnight
incident the exhausted payload was `unavailable={}` even though `opencode-go-3` had ~9h and
`opencode-go-2` ~13.9 days of reset remaining.

Additionally, `_providers_outside_window` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:1984`) only checks
`_is_within_allowed_window`, so a provider that is both quarantined and outside its window is
reported solely as `outside_time_window`, misattributing the cause.

## Change

- Add usage-limit quarantine to the exhaustion payload/`unavailable` map with remaining reset
  seconds and a distinct status/reason (e.g. `usage_limit_reset`).
- When recording diagnostics, prefer the true skip reason: quarantine before window.
- Ensure `_compute_retry_after` reflects the soonest real availability across cooldowns,
  windows and quarantine (it already reads `_usage_reset_at`; verify it is surfaced in the
  response).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An exhausted chain with a quarantined account includes that account (and its reset
      seconds) in `unavailable_providers`/`diagnostics` with a `usage_limit_reset` status.
- [ ] A provider that is both quarantined and outside its window is reported once, with
      `usage_limit_reset` as the reason.
- [ ] `retry_after` is > 0 and consistent with the soonest of cooldown/window/quarantine.
- [ ] Tests cover quarantine-only, quarantine+window, and quarantine+cooldown mixes.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:4106`, `:1984`, `:3190`, `:3279`
- Related: LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ (GoUsageLimitError reset), LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW (account keying)
data.title: Exhaustion diagnostics: expose usage-limit quarantine and derive retry_after from it

# Chain-hold cycles re-run provider resolution but never re-run session handling / compaction

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO (overnight remote-chain exhaustion epic)
**Discovered-from:** LP-0MU5A4QBR003YJM0, LP-0MU5A84YU003YOTY (live observation
2026-09-17, mode=cheap)

## Problem

When a fallback chain is exhausted, the chain-hold path holds the request for
`chain_hold_seconds` (300) and then **re-runs the chain from the first
provider**, up to `chain_hold_max_cycles` (3). The chain re-run re-emits
`routing_check`, `context_pressure`, `routing_skip_local`, the per-provider
skips and the exhaustion lines — but it does **not** re-run prompt-assembly /
session handling (`_handle_session`), which is where compaction is evaluated.

Consequences:

1. **Frozen estimates.** The routing estimate is computed at prompt-assembly,
   before the first cycle, and reused verbatim on every cycle. Observed
   identical values across every retry — e.g. session
   `herdr-1789624362-3349008-20714` logged `estimated_tokens=60753 messages=52`
   at 08:22:05, 08:27:05, 08:32:05 … 09:41:12 (exactly 300 s apart), and
   `herdr-1789599605-2754552-6910` / `herdr-1789604501-3027030-30705` likewise
   never changed (`48473`, `65138`).
2. **Compaction is attempted at most once — permanently.** `_handle_session`
   runs once per client request. If it resolves to `remote_with_guidance`
   (summarizer failed), no cycle re-attempts compaction, so a summarizer that
   becomes available — or a session that later crosses the trigger — never
   recovers for the whole hold. Session `…30705` attempted compaction once
   (08:22:09, `summarizer_failed`), then re-logged the identical
   `routing_check` at 09:33:02 and 09:38:02 with no further attempt.
3. **Observability hazard.** Each cycle re-emits an identical-looking
   `routing_check`/`routing_skip_local` pair for the *same* request. Downstream
   consumers cannot distinguish a 300 s hold cycle from a new client request,
   so `proxy-usage-analysis` demand/fallback counters are inflated and the
   repeated lines read as "the client keeps retrying" when it may be one held
   request.

## Evidence distinguishing cycles from new requests

For a genuine new request the log shows the session machinery between the
routing line and the dispatch, e.g. session `herdr-1789633820-1816851-15310`
at 09:33:19:

```
routing_check ... estimated_tokens=5871 ... messages=8 session=herdr-...-15310
Session header resolved: source=session_id session=herdr-17...
cache_invalidation: full re-process required - delta_disabled (force_full_prompt=True)
Session herdr-17... history match=True delta_messages=1 using full prompt
[local] POST http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1/chat/completions ...
```

For the held sessions' cycles, the routing line is followed **only** by
provider skips and the exhaustion/hold lines — no `Session header resolved`,
no `history match`, no compaction line ever.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Confirm or refute the mechanism.** Add a correlation id / explicit log for
   each chain-hold cycle and each `_handle_session` invocation; a test (or a
   documented reproduction) states exactly how many times session handling and
   compaction run for a single held request across N cycles. The finding above
   is an inference from the 300 s cadence, the frozen estimates and the missing
   session-handling lines — it must be proven, not assumed.
- [ ] **Decide and document the intended semantics.** Either (a) each chain cycle
   re-evaluates compaction when the session is over the trigger, or (b) it is
   intentionally evaluated once and that is stated in the code/docstring with
   the rationale. No silent middle ground.
- [ ] **If (a): a summarizer failure must not pin the request for the whole hold.**
   A cycle in which compaction can now succeed must compact (or refresh the
   guidance), and the dispatched body must reflect the compacted history.
- [ ] **Observability.** Hold-cycle re-emissions are distinguishable from genuine
   new requests in `proxy.log` and in `proxy-usage-analysis` counters (e.g. a
   `chain_hold_cycle=N` field, or a sticky request id on the routing line), so
   repeated `routing_check` lines are not counted as new demand.
- [ ] **Reused-estimate visibility.** The reused (frozen) estimate is either
   refreshed per cycle or explicitly logged as reused, so repeated identical
   `estimated_tokens` values are self-explanatory rather than looking like a
   stuck cache.
- [ ] **Regression test** asserting a deterministic number of `routing_check`
   emissions and compaction evaluations for one held request across
   `chain_hold_max_cycles`.

## Out of scope / related

- Bounding the **hold duration** by `retry_after` — LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08
  (existing child of this epic).
- Emitting a window-specific 503 — LP-0MU56ZFII004L7OO.
- Why compaction fails in the first place — LP-0MU570JAA006LMID,
  LP-0MU5A84YU003YOTY.
- Why the session is bypassed from local at all — LP-0MU5A4QBR003YJM0.
data.title: Chain-hold cycles re-run provider resolution but never re-run session handling / compaction

data.description:
## Goal

As the proxy maintainer, cancel the in-flight upstream httpx stream when the
local-dispatch no-progress watchdog releases a dispatch record, so the
llama-server slot and GPU are actually freed (parent LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8).

Without this, the watchdog releases only proxy-side bookkeeping and the orphaned
prefill keeps the slot wedged until a proxy restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When the no-progress watchdog releases a local dispatch record, the
  in-flight upstream request for that session is cancelled (httpx stream
  closed) within a bounded time; a unit test using a stub upstream asserts the
  cancellation hook is invoked.
- AC3: The watchdog path is counter-clean: `local_active_queries` and
  `active_queries` return to 0 as part of the release, with no subsequent
  counter-recovered reconciliation event (test asserts no reconciliation
  warning is emitted).
- AC5: Cancellation is idempotent and safe against the normal completion race
  (no spurious errors logged, no double-decrement); test covers
  watchdog-fires-just-as-request-completes.
- AC6: Full suite green via `/skill:test`.

## Implementation notes

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`: after the stream opens
  (`cm, response = await _await_first_byte_with_prefill_monitor(...)`), store
  `cm` on the dispatch record
  (`srv.local_dispatch_records[record_key]["stream_cm"] = cm`).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: in `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` phase 1,
  collect watchdog-released records; after releasing the records lock, close
  each `stream_cm` via `await cm.__aexit__(None, None, None)` (the deferred-I/O
  pattern already used for phases 2/3), guarded so it is idempotent and never
  raises.
- Do NOT cancel the pending `_stream_iter` future (explicit CRITICAL
  constraint: cancelling an in-flight httpx read destroys the connection).
- Do not weaken the progress-aware lease extension (genuine long prefills that
  advance must not be aborted).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_watchdog_upstream_cancellation.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_anonymous_adaptive_lease.py` (fixture/pattern reference)

## Deliverables

- `stream_cm` tracked on the dispatch record and closed on watchdog release.
- Unit tests: cancellation hook invoked; counter cleanliness; idempotency.
data.title: Cancel upstream stream on watchdog release (unit slice)

Parent: LP-0MUI5B98B0080CIB (epic) — Stream finish errors: adopt recovery-first + informative-error strategy

## Goal

Derive a deterministic root cause for every `stream_finish_error` / `stream_error` event and carry it into the report artifacts, so residual errors are attributable without grepping logs.

## Context

The stale report recommendation fires whenever `stream_finish_error > 0` and has no root-cause split. The fixture window 2026-09-25 05:00 → 2026-09-26 05:00 (`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-09-27/`) has **31** `stream_finish_error` events: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash `stall_after_content` **24**, local/Qwen3 `stream_exception` **6** (restart-correlated), deepseek/deepseek-flash `stream_exception` **1**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Root-cause classification is surfaced: each stream_finish_error event carries a root_cause.
- Proxy restart markers are parsed into timestamped log events by log_parser.py, with unit tests.
- The classification appears in errors.csv (root_cause column) and errors.json (root-cause breakdown), entirely data-driven.
- A fixture test over the 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-26 window asserts the 24/6/1 split, and a missing-marker fixture degrades to other.

## Classification rules (initial, validated against the fixture)

- `root_cause` values: `upstream_stall_after_content`, `mode_switch_restart`, `remote_chain_exhaustion`, `other`.
- `upstream_stall_after_content`: `error_type == "stall_after_content"` (idle timeout after content — re-route impossible).
- `mode_switch_restart`: provider `local` AND a restart/mode-switch marker within N seconds before the event (N documented; evidence: 17:27:58 restart → 2 kills at 17:28:00; 14:10:19 → 1; 10:00 scheduled switch → 3).
- `remote_chain_exhaustion`: remote-provider stream error with no restart correlation and no `stall_after_content`.
- `other`: anything else (graceful degradation when restart markers are missing).

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first: fixtures for restart markers, each class, the 24/6/1 window, and the degrade-to-`other` case.
2. Parse restart markers in `log_parser.py`.
3. Add `root_cause` to `LogEvent`; classify in `aggregation.py`.
4. Surface in `reporting.py` (`ERROR_CSV_COLUMNS`, `_error_row`, `error_provider_model_json`).

## Dependencies

None (foundational; F2 and F3 depend on this).

## Deliverables

Code + tests + updated CSV/JSON schema in the `proxy-usage-analysis` skill.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — Parse restart/mode-switch markers and add `root_cause` to `LogEvent`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Compute and store the per-event classification.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Emit `root_cause` in `errors.csv` / `errors.json`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — Fixture tests for rules and the 24/6/1 split.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — New restart-marker and error-event fixtures.
data.title: Classify stream-finish error root causes

# Extend prompt_cache_analysis.py with throughput + client-visible first-byte latency (AC6)

Follow-up to LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L (prompt-cache right-sizing). That item's AC1
artifact (`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`) measures cache/prefill counters
but not the two throughput/latency metrics AC6 needs to prove "no regression":

- **Generation throughput (decode tok/s)** — present in llama-server logs as
  `eval time = ... N tokens per second` lines, but not parsed here.
- **Prompt-eval throughput (tok/s)** — `prompt eval time = ...` lines; the
  interim 118.4 -> 103.8 tok/s figure was computed by hand.
- **Client-visible first-byte latency** — proxy-side metric logged by the
  proxy as `dispatch_first_byte_ms=...` (LP-0MTJET616005S7PN); not parsed here.

No new proxy log line is strictly required: both proxy-side first-byte and
llama-server throughput data already exist in the logs. The gap is that the
AC1/AC5/AC6 measurement artifact ignores them.

## Goal

Give the prompt-cache measurement a throughput + first-byte-latency section so
the cache-ram upgrade can be verified (AC6) with a reproducible before/after
artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` parses llama-server `eval time =` lines
   (decode) and `prompt eval time =` lines (prompt-eval) and reports tok/s
   stats (samples, median, p10, p90) in both the human summary and `--json`.
2. It parses proxy `dispatch_first_byte_ms=` lines (proxy.log plus rotated /
   gzipped siblings) and reports first-byte latency stats (samples, median,
   p10, p90). Default proxy log dir `/var/log/llama-proxy`, overridable.
3. `meta` records the proxy log corpus so the window is reproducible.
4. Multi-pattern `--glob` (comma-separated) and/or `--cache-ram-filter MIB` so
   the post-deploy corpus (several rotated llama-server files) is selectable
   without a hand-built symlink directory (folds in LP-0MUQOQ5C80060SH6).
5. Unit tests over synthetic llama-server + proxy logs assert the new metric
   contract; existing `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py` still passes.
6. Documented in `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` (runbook updated).
7. Full project test suite passes.
data.title: Extend prompt_cache_analysis.py with throughput + client-visible first-byte latency (AC6)
